summary: Veritas is evaluating Redwood for low-latency inference for trading/risk alerts. Primary goals: achieve p95 latency ~250ms for short chat-like requests at concurrency ~50-100, support streaming token output, and run token/sec benchmarks on customer prompts. Security requires SOC2 and KMS; exploring Dedicated (reserved GPU) or Private deployment for data residency. Redwood SE to run benchmarks and provide sizing/pricing.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
[00:06] Lena: Hi, I'm Lena, head of ML at Veritas. we're exploring ways to move our alerting models off of our noisy self-hosted infra.
[00:12] Marco: Marco, platform eng, I'll own integration.
[00:15] Sofia: Sofia, security.
[00:18] Ravi: Ravi Patel, SE at Redwood. i'll dig into the perf bits.
[00:24] Maya: Goal for today's call is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming needs, and then outline a benchmark plan.
[00:33] Lena: Our primary requirement is p95 latency ~250ms for short inference (around 40-80 token replies) under ~50 concurrent requests sustained, burst to 200 for market open. We also need streaming so the UI updates token-by-token.
[00:50] Marco: To add, peak QPS might be up to 400 for short windowed alerts but sustained is lower. we can provide traffic profile.
[00:58] Ravi: Got it. couple clarifying q's — are those 250ms p95 for cold requests or warm (with KV cache)?
[01:04] Lena: Ideally warm; we can warm some prefixes but not everything. hope caching + batching helps.
[01:09] Maya: And how important is cost vs latency? any hard constraints on monthly commit?
[01:14] Lena: Cost matters, but latency is more critical for customer-facing alerts. we'll consider reserved capacity if it guarantees SLOs.
[01:21] Sofia: Security — we need SOC2 evidence, our keys managed in our KMS, and SSO (SAML). data residency in us-east only.
[01:29] Ravi: Redwood supports SAML SSO and KMS integrations, and our Private option can run in VPC or on-prem for residency. For latency: p95 250ms with streaming at concurrency 50 is feasible with dedicated H100-class nodes depending on model size and quantization.
[01:45] Marco: Which models are you recommending? we currently run a fine-tuned 13B-ish model for summarization/alerts.
[01:52] Ravi: 13B family is a good fit. with q4_0 or q4_K_mixed quantization we can hit good perf. For example, on H100 we expect ~ -- actually, hmm, approximate numbers: single-token generation latency for 13B with small context might be in the 30-50ms range per token; end-to-end for 60 tokens streamed could be ~1.5-3s naive, but with continuous batching and KV cache p95 can be brought down. For p95 250ms for whole response you'd want shorter replies or a model/architecture optimization.
[02:25] Lena: oh that's important — our alerts are typically 20-60 tokens. 250ms p95 for 40 tokens seems tight if you sum token times. are you saying it's not realistic?
[02:34] Ravi: It's a tradeoff. If you want whole-response p95 250ms for 40 tokens, that's roughly 6ms/token which is tough unless you use smaller distilled models or extremely optimized runtime and higher-cost instances. Alternative is streaming p95 250ms to first token and then smooth subsequent tokens; users often accept quick first-byte latency.
[02:50] Maya: note for sales — we position streaming-first latency vs whole-response p95.
[02:55] Marco: First-byte streaming is ok, but our SLA requires that the application shows the alert fast; if first token arrives at 200ms and rest streams that's acceptable.
[03:03] Sofia: From security standpoint, we prefer private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and customer KMS. can't send any PII to hosted multi-tenant without DPA review.
[03:12] Ravi: Understood. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and private networking. Private on-prem is also an option but adds ops. For benchmarking, we recommend running both H100 and A100 profiles, plus a Hosted run to show delta.
[03:27] Lena: Can you walk through how you measure p95 in your benchmarks?
[03:30] Ravi: sure — we measure end-to-end request latency including network hop from app->inference, decoding time, first-byte and last-byte, and also token/sec throughput under sustained concurrency. we run synthetic and customer-prompt sets; we sample tail latencies and p95/p99. For streaming we capture first-token p95 and per-token inter-arrival stats.
[03:53] Marco: What's continuous batching? we worry about added latency.
[03:57] Ravi: continuous batching groups concurrent requests into microbatches with short windowing (tens of ms) so throughput increases with minimal added latency. you can tune batch window to trade latency. Redwood's runtime also supports prefix/KV caching so repeated contexts don't re-compute earlier tokens.
[04:16] Lena: any notes about quantization or kernel choices? we have some compliance about model fidelity.
[04:20] Ravi: We can run quantized variants like 4-bit Q4 with validation set to ensure quality. kernel selection (tensor cores, custom fused kernels) matters; our runtime auto-selects optimized kernels by model/seq length. we'll include quality regression checks in benchmarks.
[04:37] Marco: For concurrency 50 sustained, what GPU count?
[04:40] Ravi: ballpark — for 13B at q4 on H100, a single H100 node can handle dozens of concurrent streaming users depending on request length; i'd estimate 50 conc might need 2-4 GPUs for comfortable p95s and headroom. We'll produce sizing after we run token/sec tests with your payloads.
[04:58] Maya: note — Dedicated offers committed nodes and burst capacity; we can show pricing tiers.
[05:04] Lena: Good. on streaming — how do you handle partial failures and fallbacks?
[05:09] Ravi: Redwood has smart routing & fallback: if a Dedicated pool is constrained, requests can be routed to a compatible model variant in Hosted or a smaller model. also automatic retry with checkpointing for streaming.
[05:21] Sofia: audit logs and traceability? we need per-request audit logs.
[05:24] Ravi: yes, we support audit logs, per-token cost breakdowns in Console, and tracing hooks. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[05:34] Marco: ok next, on benchmarking — what's the deliverable? spreadsheets? raw traces?
[05:38] Ravi: deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, token/sec, first-byte latency, config details (GPU type, quant, batch windows), and raw traces if you want. We'll also include runbook to reproduce.
[05:52] Lena: we'll provide prompt set and a representative traffic file.
[05:56] Maya: timeline — SE runs benchmarks by 3/12, we review wk of 3/15 for deep dive.
[06:02] Marco: one more — any constraints about VPC peering / egress?
[06:05] Ravi: Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private deployment can be fully in your VPC; egress policies and allow lists are supported.
[06:13] Maya: ok let's recap action items.
[06:16] Sofia: quick question about encryption at rest: does Redwood accept customer-managed keys?
[06:19] Ravi: yes, KMS integration and HSM options for private deployment.
[06:24] Lena: are you able to run a streaming-first benchmark that measures first-byte p95 and inter-token arrival? that's our priority.
[06:31] Ravi: absolutely — we'll include first-byte p95 and streaming cadence metrics.
[06:35] Maya: Cool. Any other competitors you're evaluating?
[06:38] Lena: We're also looking at Anthropic and Bedrock and some self-hosted infra. cost and ops are big differentiators.
[06:45] Maya: Understood. we'll send SOC2/security pack and pricing, and SE will run benchmarks.
[06:50] Marco: thanks, we'll share traffic and prompt file by tomorrow.
[06:54] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for deep dive.
[06:58] (call ends)
